title: Research: n=3 precision-blind dual-scale Norm on end support (answers #4070 OQ1 for n=3; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Answers open question 1 of just-open [#4070](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4070) **for n=3**: does the dual-scale reciprocal construction extend to precision-blind lists of length `n>2` with middle coordinates forced to `±1`?

**Yes for n=3**, with a new end-support analysis (not a copy of the n=2 coordinate pair):

- On `(Z/p^w Z)^3` with `a=(a0,m,1)`, `a0=1+p^{w-1}`, `m∈{±1}`, dual scales `(s_{H2},s_{D0})=(a0^{-1},a0)` on support `(H'_2,D'_0)` realize `F_{(a0,m,a0^{-1})}` with `(P')²=I`.
- The naive n=2 support `(H'_1,D'_0)` is **never** involutory: any compatible `P'` forces `p0·p2=a0≢1`.
- Single-factor on the end support remains obstructed (`a0≢±1`). `a0` is always a unit QR; existence uses invertibility, not a square root.

Algebraic for all odd `p`, `w≥2`, both middle signs. Certificate grid: 30 rows (15 `(p,w)` × `±1`). **No Boolean meters. No reprint of the #4070 15-pair n=2 census. No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`. `n≥5` left open.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale/`
- Tip: `864c38a5c5098c8506ceba48a78ee6171c7b8742`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — n=3 end-support dual-scale + naive-support obstruction answering #4070 OQ1 for n=3

Closest prior: [#4070](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4070); [#4063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4063); [#2950](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2950). Soft overlap vs #4070: semantic ≈0.40 / harness ≈0.80 (template kinship; load-bearing delta is end support + naive obstruction, not a 15-pair census reprint).

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_PRECISION_BLIND_N3_DUAL_SCALE pairs=30 primes=[3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23] widths=[2, 3, 4, 5] support=(H'_2,D'_0) middles=±1 single_factor=0 naive_n2=0 square=always dual_scales=inv boolean_meters=false n2_census=false no_new_kappa
PASS_INDEPENDENT_PRECISION_BLIND_N3_DUAL_SCALE pairs=30 support=(H'_2,D'_0) middles=±1 single_factor=0 naive_n2=0 square=always dual_scales=inv boolean_meters=false n2_census=false no_new_kappa
PASS_PRECISION_BLIND_N3_DUAL_SCALE_PACKAGE_TESTS groups=6
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/precision-blind-n3-dual-scale outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Open next questions / limitations

1. Does the same end-support pattern certify every odd length `n=2k+1≥5` with independent `±1` middles?
2. A fully charged Boolean inventory for one n=3 `(p,w,m)` would need a new length-3 fixture — leave-alone policy blocks thin meter retargets.
3. The naive-support check is structural (`False` for all scales), not a scale-search census.
